correctness.rationale: PASS: Q is unimodular and Q^7=I+2B, Q^14=I+4D with det(B)=det(D)=1. Squaring shows the exact primitive period T_k=7·2^(k-1), giving N_k=4^(k-1) cycles. For lag h not divisible by 7 the two observation rows remain independent mod 2; for h=7t their common 2-adic content is 2^(1+v_2(t)), which leads to primitive solution count C_h=2^(k+hval-1). Summing the six ordinary lag classes and k-1 2-adic valuation classes gives E Z_k=3, E Z_k²=k+8, Var=k-1. Independently enumerated all primitive cycles for k=1..4 and checked exact first two moments, including k=1 boundary. This does not prove the infinite period lifting by enumeration.
residual_risks: All k≥1, exactly recurrence modulo powers of two; nonprimitive states and distribution beyond first two moments excluded.
